$comment: Benchlee demo dataset. Every run below is seeded with provenance='demo' and is
rendered in the UI behind a 'Demo dataset' badge. The artifacts are hand-authored
fixtures that exist to exercise the product surface — they are NOT transcripts of
real API calls, and the site says so on every page.
To publish real results, run `pnpm bench:run` with provider API keys set; that
writes rows with provenance='live', which render without the demo badge.
This file is meant to be edited: add a model here, drop matching artifact files

models.notes: Long-context multimodal model from Google DeepMind.

tasks.title: The Pricing Page
tasks.summary: Three tiers, one page, no framework. The task every model claims to ace and most quietly botch.
tasks.why_it_matters: A pricing page is a taste test disguised as a layout exercise. Spacing, hierarchy, and the courage to make one tier louder than the others are all visible in two seconds — and none of it shows up in a numeric score.
tasks.prompt: Write a single self-contained HTML file for a SaaS pricing page. Three tiers: Solo ($0), Studio ($24/mo), Scale ($96/mo). Dark theme. No external CSS, no JS frameworks, no images, no network requests. Highlight the middle tier as the recommended plan. It must look finished.

tasks.title: The Chart, By Hand
tasks.summary: Given eight numbers, draw an honest chart in raw SVG. No chart library to hide behind.
tasks.why_it_matters: Charting libraries paper over whether a model understands scale, baselines and label collision. Hand-rolled SVG does not. This is where you see if the model can do arithmetic and design at the same time.
tasks.prompt: Write a single self-contained HTML file containing a hand-authored inline SVG chart of quarterly revenue: 2024 Q1 1.2, Q2 1.9, Q3 2.4, Q4 3.1, 2025 Q1 3.0, Q2 4.4, Q3 5.1, Q4 6.8 (millions USD). Bars for each quarter plus a line showing the trend. Include axis labels, gridlines and a title. No libraries, no external requests.

tasks.title: No-JavaScript Clock
tasks.summary: An analog clock whose hands actually move, with the JavaScript escape hatch nailed shut.
tasks.why_it_matters: Take away the obvious tool and you find out whether a model reasons about a medium or pattern-matches on it. Correct CSS animation timing (60s, 3600s, 43200s) is a fact you can verify by watching it.
tasks.prompt: Write a single self-contained HTML file showing an analog clock face with hour, minute and second hands that animate continuously using CSS only. No JavaScript at all. The second hand must sweep once per minute, the minute hand once per hour, the hour hand once per twelve hours. Include the twelve hour markers.

tasks.title: 404 With A Personality
tasks.summary: An open brief with one hard rule: be memorable without being annoying.
tasks.why_it_matters: Open briefs separate models with taste from models with a template. There is no right answer here, which is exactly why a leaderboard number can't settle it and two artifacts side by side can.
tasks.prompt: Write a single self-contained HTML file for a 404 page with genuine personality. Dark theme, one clear route back to the homepage. Be memorable but not obnoxious — no autoplay, no flashing, nothing that would annoy a user who is already lost. No external assets.
